svg.title: From Retired Device to Accepted Resale
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-traceable-resale-workflow; chart type: process_flow; title: From Retired Device to Accepted Resale; subtitle: Five evidence-backed stages for diagnostic, surgical, veterinary, and aesthetic equipment.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Stage values indicate sequence, not elapsed time or conversion. The canonical time to first deal is 3–9 months. Inventory tracking and service-history indexing automate records, not physical testing or device-specific regulatory classification.; caption: Keep one serial-level record from sourcing through buyer acceptance; never substitute a cosmetic refurbishment claim for functional evidence.; stages: label: Source against demand; value: 1 | Buyer need and asset identity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record model, serial number, intended use, accessories, software revision, asking price, and two dated buyer-demand observations. Check recalls and service support before committing inventory cash.; label: Establish transfer rights; value: 2 | Ownership and disposition evidence; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Match seller authority to the serial list, inspect relevant UCC filings, and obtain required secured-party release or disposition authorization. UCC 9-315 means sale alone does not necessarily remove a security interest.; label: Quarantine and sanitize; value: 3 | Separate biological and data controls; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Require device-compatible decontamination documentation and inspect every data-bearing component. Record sanitization method and verification separately; do not assume a factory reset removes stored patient records or that surface cleaning addresses internal contamination.; label: Restore and verify; value: 4 | Qualified biomed acceptance evidence; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use model-specific test procedures, calibrated instruments, parts traceability, and measured acceptance limits. Evaluate servicing versus remanufacturing before changes to performance, safety specifications, or intended use; investigate duties under 21 CFR Parts 807 and 820 when triggered.; label: Deliver and close; value: 5 | Settled proceeds and buyer acceptance; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Confirm site readiness, insured freight, installation scope, payment settlement, and signed acceptance. Archive test results, transfer records, warranty terms, and service history against the serial number; recognize equipment resale proceeds rather than treating refundable deposits as completed revenue.

rect.title: label: Source against demand; value: 1 | Buyer need and asset identity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record model, serial number, intended use, accessories, software revision, asking price, and two dated buyer-demand observations. Check recalls and service support before committing inventory cash.

text.title: Record model, serial number, intended use, accessories, software revision, asking price, and two dated buyer-demand observations. Check recalls and service support before committing inventory cash.

rect.title: label: Establish transfer rights; value: 2 | Ownership and disposition evidence; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Match seller authority to the serial list, inspect relevant UCC filings, and obtain required secured-party release or disposition authorization. UCC 9-315 means sale alone does not necessarily remove a security interest.

text.title: Match seller authority to the serial list, inspect relevant UCC filings, and obtain required secured-party release or disposition authorization. UCC 9-315 means sale alone does not necessarily remove a security interest.

rect.title: label: Quarantine and sanitize; value: 3 | Separate biological and data controls; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Require device-compatible decontamination documentation and inspect every data-bearing component. Record sanitization method and verification separately; do not assume a factory reset removes stored patient records or that surface cleaning addresses internal contamination.

text.title: Require device-compatible decontamination documentation and inspect every data-bearing component. Record sanitization method and verification separately; do not assume a factory reset removes stored patient records or that surface cleaning addresses internal contamination.

rect.title: label: Restore and verify; value: 4 | Qualified biomed acceptance evidence; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use model-specific test procedures, calibrated instruments, parts traceability, and measured acceptance limits. Evaluate servicing versus remanufacturing before changes to performance, safety specifications, or intended use; investigate duties under 21 CFR Parts 807 and 820 when triggered.

text.title: Use model-specific test procedures, calibrated instruments, parts traceability, and measured acceptance limits. Evaluate servicing versus remanufacturing before changes to performance, safety specifications, or intended use; investigate duties under 21 CFR Parts 807 and 820 when triggered.

rect.title: label: Deliver and close; value: 5 | Settled proceeds and buyer acceptance; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Confirm site readiness, insured freight, installation scope, payment settlement, and signed acceptance. Archive test results, transfer records, warranty terms, and service history against the serial number; recognize equipment resale proceeds rather than treating refundable deposits as completed revenue.

text.title: Confirm site readiness, insured freight, installation scope, payment settlement, and signed acceptance. Archive test results, transfer records, warranty terms, and service history against the serial number; recognize equipment resale proceeds rather than treating refundable deposits as completed revenue.

Assumptions: Stage values indicate sequence, not elapsed time or conversion. The canonical time to first deal is 3–9 months. Inventory tracking and service-history indexing automate records, not physical testing or device-specific regulatory classification.
